question: Is the 512-to-576 MiB hit-rate cliff specific to LRU on the recorded routes, or unavoidable at that byte budget?

relaxedOracleBound.scope: Equal-size mandatory-admission demand paging with route pins relaxed; a miss lower bound, not a deployable policy.

independentLRUCheck: Compute distinct intervening expert reuse distances and verify each LRU hit count against its integer expert capacity.

execution.accessOrder: Recorded step-major layer order and recorded selected-expert order, never sorted.
execution.pinning: Each successfully loaded demand expert stays protected until the end of its eight-expert layer record; future selected experts are not protected before demand.
execution.phases: One continuous prefill-to-decode run. Phase counters are deltas in that run; no decode cache reset.
execution.randomChoice: Python random.Random(seed), uniform over currently unprotected resident keys in dictionary insertion order.
execution.lfu: Per-residency demand frequency; ties by last access, then stable insertion order.
execution.hybrid: Per-residency frequency divided by (1 + current access clock - last access); ties by last access, then stable insertion order.
execution.oracle: Existing farthest-next-use eviction with the same route pin constraints. Any relaxed unpinned Belady bound must be reported separately; do not presume pin-constrained optimality.

validation: All five 576 MiB LRU baselines must exactly reproduce captured device hits, misses, and logical payload bytes.
Every request is a hit or a miss; logical bytes equal misses times the fixed expert block size.
All caches stay within byte budget, with zero oversized-expert or pinned-working-set bypasses on the real suite.
All policies use exactly the same demand order and pin lifetime.
Deterministic synthetic fixtures check FIFO hit/reinsertion behavior, random seed reproducibility, protection, and farthest-next-use oracle scope.
Prefill and decode counters sum to the complete run without resetting the cache.
Keep every fixed seed and every budget; do not select only favorable random trials.

aggregates.deterministic: Report per-prompt results, prompt-equal macro mean, and request/byte-weighted micro totals.
aggregates.random: Report every seed, seed mean and range, and separately prompt-equal/request-weighted aggregates. Seeds are simulation sensitivity, not independent prompts or phone replicates.

stoppingRule: One fixed sweep; no threshold fitting, invented adaptive policy, new phone run, or rented hardware. Preserve the measured LRU baseline and all negative results.
limitations: Fixed-route cache replay does not measure wall-clock latency, storage contention, process memory, power, or output quality.
A better non-LRU hit rate at 512 MiB disproves inevitability of zero hits on these traces, not all capacity constraints or the observed LRU timing results.
Five prompts provide bounded sensitivity evidence, not a universal optimal cache budget.
Existing traces are reused after review; this protocol is fixed before this new sweep, not a claim of preregistered original data collection.
